phase: 2a — cross-cutting principles P1-P4, repo-wide, with per-file lists
method: Each ga-gate script run as `npx tsx tools/ga-gate/<x>.ts > log 2>&1; echo RC=$?`. Every gate reading was then re-derived INDEPENDENTLY with grep, and for P4 with a probe that imports the gate's OWN scanner (tools/ga-gate/lib/sourceScan.ts) so the per-file split reproduces the ENFORCED (comment-stripped) number rather than a raw line count.

scope_sanity.purpose: D4 — a gate pointed at an emptied directory reports 0 forever. Every scan dir was counted before trusting any 0.
scope_sanity.command: for d in src apps packages plugins server tools scripts apps/editor/src/engine packages/renderer-three packages/frame-scheduler; do find $d -type f \( -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' -o -name '*.js' \) | grep -v node_modules | wc -l; done
scope_sanity.verdict: MEANINGFUL for every gate EXCEPT one half of one arm. `src/` holds SIX source files (ls src/ -> boot-shell.d.ts, browser-entry.tsx, browser.css, global-window.d.ts, gpuDisabledOverlay.ts, main.ts, three-addons.d.ts; three are .d.ts and one is .css, so only browser-entry.tsx / gpuDisabledOverlay.ts / main.ts are scannable). `grep -rn 'window as any' src/` returns NOTHING. The P4 STRICT arm is declared as 'src + apps/editor/src/engine'; the src half contributes ~3 of 308 files and structurally cannot produce a finding. It is not an artefact (the engine half is 306 real files and IS producing findings) but the src half is VESTIGIAL, and the gate's own docstring concedes it: 'src/ today contains ZERO casts, so the original gate would have printed OK: 0 while 215 casts sat outside its field of view.'

findings.severity: gate blind spot (DECLARED by the gate itself)
findings.subject: The pattern is an anchored ImportDeclaration regex. Inline type-position `import('three').X` and dynamic `await import('three')` are invisible.
findings.evidence: PATTERN = /^\s*import\b.*\bfrom\s*['"]three(?:\/[^'"]+)?['"]/ at check-three-imports.ts:71. The gate's own header at line 33 lists "await import('three')  · dynamic; not an import declaration" under NOT matched.
findings.command: grep -rn --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist --exclude-dir=dist-server-deps "import(['\"]three['\"])" apps packages plugins src server tools scripts | grep -v '^packages/renderer-three/'
findings.honest_caveat: All three production sites are TYPE positions — erased at compile time, creating no runtime THREE ownership. P2's runtime invariant is intact. What is measured is that the gate's field of view is narrower than P2's sentence: a future RUNTIME `await import('three')` in these same files would pass.

findings.severity: adjacent, not a P2 violation as written

The terminal output shows the strict arm's per-file census with no pass/fail line attached, so a reader sees 'FAIL (repo-wide): 101 > 100' and concludes ONE arm is over by ONE. EVASION_FORMS_MEASURED.why: The brief's TRAP: bracket notation (window as any)['x'] evades a dot-notation grep. The gate's regex /\(\s*window\s+as\s+any\s*\)/ matches the CAST itself, so BOTH (window as any).x and (window as any)['x'] are covered — that trap is closed. The REAL escape hatch is a DIFFERENT SPELLING of the same cast, which gate-debt.json already names: 'MEASURED, NOT FIXED: 409 `window as unknown as` casts across 151 files — almost twice the 215 ceiling sitting in a spelling this gate cannot see. That blind spot needs its own ratchet before P4 can be called enforced; until then a green here means no new casts in the ONE spelling checked.' Re-measured below.
EVASION_FORMS_MEASURED.method: Same scanner (scanFilesStripped), same dirs, same test/.d.ts exclusions as the gate's repo-wide arm.

cross_cutting_findings.subject: Three of four principles' documented readings disagree with today's measurement — in BOTH directions.
cross_cutting_findings.detail: P2 documented denominator 6261, measured 8171 (doc understates coverage). P3 documented '5 owners FAILING', measured 1 owner PASS (doc is pessimistic and quotes a number retracted the following day). P4 documented 'RC=0, both arms within ceiling', measured RC=3 with both arms breached (doc is optimistic). Only P1 agrees exactly. The thing that keeps failing is not the principle — it is the hand-transcribed number.

cross_cutting_findings.subject: Two of the four gates report an architecture number their own pattern structurally cannot produce.
cross_cutting_findings.detail: P1's success line prints the LITERAL '0 rivals' beside a census of 1. P3's owner count of 1 excludes a known live rAF pump because the pattern requires a '(' after the token. In both cases the gate's own source documents the gap in a comment. A comment is not a measurement (D1).

cross_cutting_findings.subject: No gate in this set is MISCONFIGURED and no scope is emptied.
cross_cutting_findings.detail: All four ran to completion. Exit codes: P1=0, P2=0, P3=0, P4=3. No ENOENT, no exit 2, no timeout. Every scan directory is populated (see scope_sanity). The single vestigial scope is the `src/` half of P4's strict arm (3 scannable files, 0 casts) — and the engine half of that same arm carries 306 real files and is producing real findings, so it is a weak scope, not a dead one.

cross_cutting_findings.subject: Scan-dir sets are inconsistent ACROSS the four gates, and nothing reconciles them.
cross_cutting_findings.detail: check-three-imports scans src,apps,packages,plugins,server,tools,scripts (7). check-cast-count repo-wide and rafOwners scan the same minus scripts (6). check-single-compose scans src,apps,plugins,packages (4) — no server, no tools, no scripts. A file's principle coverage therefore depends on which directory it happens to live in. Measured consequence for P4: 2 real casts in scripts/ that no ratchet counts.
